finding: Anthropomorphism that personifies the gradient ('says so') and obscures the mechanism. The phrasing also misleadingly implies that the frozen base weights are eventually modified once gradients arrive, whereas the base model is permanently frozen and only adapter matrices A and B receive gradient updates.
evidence: Essay line 23 ('Nothing about the base is disturbed until the gradient says so.') contradicts line 21 ('W is marked frozen, so the backward pass computes how the loss changes with A and with B and never allocates a gradient for W') and line 37 ('the base model is never patched in place'). CONTEXT.md §4 prohibits anthropomorphism that hides the mechanism.
fix: Replace 'Nothing about the base is disturbed until the gradient says so.' with 'The base weights remain untouched throughout training; only the adapter matrices receive gradients and update.'
